newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE - World market for December 3, 1996 - Robusta futures in London ended off the day's highs after an early rally discouraged industry buyers. Front month January last traded at $1,339, up $2 while March, the most active contract, last traded up $5 at $1,293.

In New York arabica futures closed lower across the board with front month December losing 50 points to close at 114.30 cents/lb. March gave up 95 points to close at 105.10 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 50 and 90 points.

The market was largely technically driven, with players brushing aside the latest CSC certified stock data. The CSC reported after the close of business Monday that US-certified coffee stocks were unchanged at 321 60-kg bags in the week ended November 29, which was expected to aid sentiment.
Most analysts expect prices to ease further with new crop supplies coming onto the market but overall coffee is not expected to be in abundant supply throughout the season.

COLOMBIA - Colombia will produce 12.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1996/97 (October/September) which compares to 12.9 million bags the previous year, Jorge Cardenas, the head of the National Coffee Growers Federation said.

The estimate for 1996/97 is in sharp contrast to the recent estimate given by Gabriel Rosas Vega, the head of Colombia's Exporters Association, who pegged output this season at 10.5 to 11.0 million bags. Cardenas said of the total expected to be produced in 1996/97 11.5 million bags will be marked for export.
Stocks at the end of 1996/97 are expected to fall to 5.6 million bags, down from 6.1 million bags the previous year. Internal demand is put at 1.5 million bags.

One major problem for Colombian coffee producers is the constant revaluation of the peso against the US$. The Colombian coffee sector claims it has lost $2.8 billion over the past six years due to the fall in the value of the US$. Growers demand measures to be taken to offset this.

MEXICO - Mexico exported 163,489 60-kg bags of coffee in October 1996, the first year of the 1996/97 crop cycle, up from 131,912 bags exported the same month the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached the record amount of 4.579 million bags.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 79,871 bags of coffee in October 1996, 10 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 736,000 bags, 1 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar 1995 dropped by 7 per cent to 814,700 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Indonesia (129,400 vs 89,600 bags), Vietnam (142,100 vs 153,100 bags) and Papua New Guinea (206,700 vs 190,200 bags).
